children: General Motors Company (NYSE:GM) is shifting production to a next‑gen pickup platform that will cut ~35,000 trucks in Q4 as it pursues digital, defense and insurance revenue growth, targets $3B in connected services, and braces for 2027 EV margin and tariff headwinds.
Previous Week Recap
GM Production Shift Cost
: GM expects normal Q4 2026 seasonality and plans a production shift to a next‑gen pickup platform, estimating a loss of about 35,000 trucks in the quarter tied to the transition.
General Motors Outlook Reaffirmed
: General Motors (GM) reaffirmed its 2027 outlook, expecting revenue, EBIT and free cash flow growth while warning that tariffs, commodity inflation, fuel and logistics costs could affect results.
GM Targets $3 Billion Digital Revenue
: General Motors targets about $3 billion in digital revenue as connected-vehicle services and subscriptions boost earnings; Super Cruise renewal rates are roughly 30%–40% after prepaid periods.
GM Connected Services Rollout
: GM expects significant deferred revenue from connected-vehicle services and Super Cruise; plans to roll out hands-off highway driving on Escalade IQ in 2028 and expand Super Cruise to more models
GM CFO cautions 2027 EV Margin
: GM CFO Paul Jacobson warned 2027 could be tough for GM's EV unit, citing tariff and EV-credit accounting pressure on margins and stressing the need to restore sustained EV profitability.
GM Ultium Cells Pause, Rehire
: GM paused Ultium Cells battery cell production in January amid weak EV demand, idling ~850 workers and laying off ~480; production resumed mid‑August after rehiring ~700, ~600 remain on layoff
GM Defense Parts for Patriot PAC-3
: GM started shipping missile-housing parts for Lockheed Martin’s Patriot PAC-3 MSE in August, aims for ~$700M in defense revenue this year, and is in talks to supply parts for other missile lines
GM Calls Hybrids Temporary Tech
: GM calls hybrids a temporary tech. Hybrids may show up in key segments; current hybrid offering limited to Corvette. No U.S. launch timeline or updated guidance provided by GM.
GM 2027 Expansion And Onshoring

: GM plans for 2027: new truck platform, higher Orion plant capacity, onshoring moves, lower warranty costs, expanded digital revenue and growth in defense business; all internally driven initiatives.
GM Digital, Defense Diversification
: GM grew digital revenue and expanded defense and insurance businesses, boosting non-vehicle sales and diversifying revenue streams; no figures, time frames, or profit/margin details were provided.
